title: Venison Pie
subtitle: A deep British pie of slow-braised venison in a rich red wine gravy
excerpt: Tender braised venison in a dark, winey gravy, topped with a butter-glazed puff pastry lid. A weekend pie that rewards slow cooking.
sourceNotes: British game pie tradition drawing on Scottish and English moorland cookery; adapted for a 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked filling without the pastry lid. Defrost overnight, top with fresh pastry and bake.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the venison filling up to two days ahead. The flavour improves as it sits. Top with pastry and bake when needed.

content.text: Venison is lean and needs a long, slow braise to become tender. Rush it and you will get tough, chewy meat. The puff lid goes on cold filling only, so plan for the braise to be done well ahead of baking.
Pat the venison dry and season it. Dust with flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in the Dutch oven over a high heat. Brown the venison in batches for two minutes per side. Transfer each batch to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion and carrot in the same pot for eight minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato puree and stir for one minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for two minutes. Add the stock, bay leaves, thyme and juniper berries. Return the venison and any resting juices.
Cover and braise on the lowest heat for two hours, until the venison is very tender. Remove the lid for the last 20 minutes to reduce the gravy until it coats the meat. Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Spoon the cold filling into the pie dish. Lay the puff pastry over the top, trim and press the edges to the rim.
Brush with beaten egg. Cut two small slits in the top. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden.

items.symptom: The venison is tough after two hours.
items.cause: The braise boiled rather than simmered, or the pieces were too large.
items.fix: The liquid should barely tremble. Cut any large pieces down to 3cm before cooking and give it another 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The puff pastry is soggy underneath.
items.cause: The filling was warm, or the gravy was too thin.
items.fix: The filling must be cold before the pastry goes on. Reduce the gravy until it is thick before cooling.

items.symptom: The pastry lid does not rise.
items.cause: The oven was not fully preheated, or the pastry was warm before baking.
items.fix: Puff pastry needs a hot oven from the start. Keep the rolled sheet in the fridge until you are ready to lay it on.
